name: Pagination
description: Pagination moves between pages of a long list or table. It shows where people are, lets them step forward and back, and jumps to a page, shortening long ranges with an ellipsis.
whenToUse: For long lists, search results or tables split into pages.
When people need to know how much content there is and return to a specific page.

whenNotToUse.alternative: Infinite scroll or a “Load more” button

anatomy.name: Previous button
anatomy.description: Goes back one page; disabled on the first page.

anatomy.name: Current page
anatomy.description: Filled, and announced as the current page.

anatomy.name: Ellipsis
anatomy.description: Stands in for skipped pages in long ranges.

anatomy.name: Next button
anatomy.description: Goes forward one page; disabled on the last page.

values.meaning: “Page 2 of 10” between the arrows, for narrow spaces.

states.name: Default
states.meaning: A page people can go to.

states.name: Hover
states.meaning: Shows the page responds to the pointer.

states.name: Disabled
states.trigger: On the first or last page.

behavior.text: Always shows the first and last page, siblingCount pages on each side of the current one, and “…” for the rest.
Scroll to the top of the list and consider moving focus to its heading so keyboard users land on the new content.
Order and arrows follow the reading direction: “previous” points right in Arabic.

content: Keep the default labels (“Previous page”, “Next page”, “Page 3”) unless translating.
In simple mode, the summary reads “Page 2 of 10”.

guidelines.do: Show the total number of pages.
guidelines.dont: Hide how much content there is.
guidelines.why: People decide whether to keep going based on how much is left.

guidelines.do: Keep pagination in the same place on every page.
guidelines.dont: Move it around as the list length changes.
guidelines.why: A stable position lets people step through pages without hunting.

guidelines.do: Use the simple appearance where space is tight.
guidelines.dont: Let page numbers wrap onto several lines.
guidelines.why: Wrapped numbers are hard to scan and tap.

accessibility.role: navigation landmark containing a list of buttons.

keyboard.action: Moves between the arrows and page buttons.

aria.when: From label (default “Pagination”); use distinct labels if a page has two.
On the simple summary, so changes are announced.

accessibility.focus: Every button shows the focus ring when reached with the keyboard.

wcag.how: A labelled navigation landmark with a list.
Every control has a descriptive name.
Numbers pass 4.5:1 at rest, hovered and current.
The current page is exposed with aria-current.

notes: The ellipsis is hidden from screen readers; the page numbers around it are enough.

examples.title: Paging through results
examples.code:
import { Pagination } from '@ds/react';

<Pagination currentPage={page} totalPages={12} onPageChange={setPage} />

examples.title: Compact
examples.code:
import { Pagination } from '@ds/react';

<Pagination appearance="simple" currentPage={page} totalPages={12} onPageChange={setPage} />

examples.title: Translated labels
examples.description: Pass the wording for another language.

related.relation: Often paired with a paginated table.

changes: Navigation landmark, aria-current and named previous/next buttons (they had no names).
Ellipsis for long ranges (siblingCount), simple appearance, translatable labels, RTL.
The current page is now filled with the brand accent, distinct from hover.

components.name: Pagination
components.description: Moves between pages of a long list or table.

currentPage.description: The page being shown, starting at 1.

onPageChange.description: Called with the page to show.

appearance.description:
`full` (default) lists page numbers, shortening long ranges with “…”. `simple` shows
“Page 2 of 10” between the arrows, for narrow spaces.

siblingCount.description: How many pages to show on each side of the current page before “…”.

label.description: Accessible name of the navigation landmark. Default "Pagination".

labels.type: { previous?: string; next?: string; page?: ((page: number) => string) | undefined; summary?: ((page: number, total: number) => string) | undefined; } | undefined
labels.description: Accessible names and summary wording, for translation.
